newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana stocks close slightly lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Ghana stocks close slightly lower in thin trade.

text.p: Ghana's Stock Exchange index slipped further on Monday as market heavyweight Ashanti Goldfields Company lost ground, dealers said.
Small-lot selling by individual investors and public funds also contributed to the 9.25 point slide in the GSE All-Share Index from Friday's close at 376.33 points, they added.
The dealers blamed a bearish world gold market for Ashanti's loss of 2,000 cedis to 25,000 cedis.

A broker at Accra firm Databank said there was no apparent domestic factor to explain Ashanti's slide. The stock's performance on the Ghana bourse also reflected pressure seen on exchanges in London and New York, where Ashanti is also listed.
"AGC's value is now seen in the global context and whatever happens to it on these exchanges, will have a bearing here," said the broker.
AGC opened lower in London before trading began in Accra.

Two other stocks declined -- Ghana Commercial Bank Ltd lost 39 cedis to 730 cedis and Fan Milk Ltd declined three cedis to 405. The only gainer was Pioneer Tobacco Co which added one cedi to 129 cedis.
Volume was 31,320 shares traded, compared with Friday's 27,390.
Market capitalisation dropped to 2,818.82 billion cedis from 3,015.76 billion cedis.
